page.layout: One printed page, running text in a single column. Top: running text, full width, continued from the previous page. Below: the approbations (censurae), set in italic, one paragraph each. Then a decorative band, the title block (centred), the list of the subscribing theologians, and the body text with a large woodcut initial R. Margin: left, printed line numbers 5 to 60; right, the marginal note "Anno 1606" beside the title and a note beside the list.

main_text.p: 5Properans itaq; ad conclusionem; dico, Rempubl. tot & tam validas suæ partis rationes habere, quæ ipsam in hoc negotio etiam ne minimum quidem errorem commisisse facile conuincere possint; & peccasset sane; si quicquam factorum omisisset, siquidem in bona gubernatione subditorum defecisset, & suæ ipsius paci ac tranquillitati male consuluisset. Quapropter à Pontifice legitime culpari sese haud putat bonitati causæ confidens; quia sane freta omnes Principes & populos à suis partibus haud dubie habebit; [?]nec dubitat sane quin & ipse Pontifex proprio suo consilio ab omni falsa falsariorum suasione alieno tandem cogniturus, reique bonæ iustas causas & infallibiles rationes recepturus sit, cui Deus Opt. Max. benefaciat, vt ad beneficium commune nominis Christiani cedat; Amen.
main_text.head: CENSVRÆ PRÆSTANTIVM VIRORVM.

p.i: Ego Petrus Antonius Ribettus Archidiaconus, Vicarius generalis, scriptum præsens approbo, nihilque fidei catholicæ contrarium in eo contineri affirmo.
Ego Frat. Paulus, Serenissimæ Reipubl. Venetæ Theologus præsens, scriptum legi & examinavi, illudque fidei catholicæ conforme adinveni.
Ego Fr. Bernhardus Cordanus Ordinis B. Francisci idem affirmo.
Ego Fr. Michael Angelus Bonicellus Venetus Theologiæ Professor ordinis Minorum idem attestor.
Ego Fr. Camillus Venetus ordinis D. Augustinii iam dictis assentio.
Ego Marcus Antonius Peregrinus D. & Eques ac Gymnasii Patauini iuriũ Professor primarius præsens scriptum vidi, cum consideratione perlegi, & terminis rationis conuenientes offendi.
Ego Marcus Antonius Otthelius Iuris ciuilis Professor in Gymnasio Patauino ordinarius, quantum ad terminos legales pertinet, idem affirmo.
Ego Ioachimus Scaiinus[?] Professor iuris ciuilis Gymnasii Patauini dictis iubens subscribo.

DE INTERDICTO PAV-LI V. PONTIFICIS, IN QVA DEMONSTRATVR, QVOD LEGITIME NON sit publicatum, & propterea ob multas causas Ecclesiasticos ad sui executionem non obligret, nec etiam absque peccato ab iisdem possit observari;

main_text.p: 5055REQVIRIT sane, quod quisque in cultu diuino & cura propriæ salutis regi debet, zelus in hoc præsertim tempore, quo controuersiæ quam maximæ inter Pontificem & serenissimam Rempub. agitantur, vt has duas inprimis quæstiones diligenter examinando decidamus.
An scilicet Ecclesiastici debeant aut possint interdictum huius status sine peccato obseruare? Et an Princeps Venetus possit & debeat, vt ad defen-sionem, talem obseruationem prohibere?

60Ad probandum, quod Ecclesiastici huius status ad illius obseruationem sint obligati, & quod Princeps etiam debeat in id consentire, putant aliqui se satis præstitisse, si demonstrauerint, quod vnusquisq; obligatus sit ad iustis præceptis Papæ obediendi. Ad quod probandum, multum & nostra quidem opinione extra rem ac superflue laborant: siquidem non hoc solummodo illis concedimus, sed etiam quod Episcoporum iustis præceptis obedientiam omnino debeamus, quemadmodum etiam Principibus & bonis Magistratui eadem haud quaquam recusanda est, &

page.notes: Printed line numbers in the left margin (5 to 60) are transcribed as notes at their lines. The woodcut band between the censure and the title is ornament only and is not transcribed. The top-left edge of the scan shows show-through from the facing page and is omitted. Doubtful readings: "[?]nec" (the printed word may be "hoc" or "nec"), "Scaiinus" (possible spelling variant), the right-margin note "Auctor scripti est" (the word "scripti" is hard to read), and the catchword "vi" at the bottom right, which may be a catchword or a page signature. The signature "EE" is centred at the foot. The printed line numbers are placed at the paragraph where their line falls, which is approximate.
